name: emit_readout
description: TrialScout readout, schema v4. Two tiers with a hard line between them. The `facts` tier is READ from the ClinicalTrials.gov record by schema/facts.py and is never requested from a model -- it is what the registry states. The remaining fields are what the registry only implies, and those are the model's job. v4 moves `phase`, `sponsor_type` and `est_readout` across that line: all three are stated or arithmetic, all three scored 0.97-1.00 under v3, and asking for them inflated the headline with lookups. See ADR-0024.

nct_id.description: Registry identifier. Copied from the record.

facts.description: Everything the registry states outright, extracted by schema/facts.py. NEVER generated. Fields are omitted when the registry is silent -- absence means 'not stated', which is itself information, and is never filled with a guess.

sponsor.description: Lead sponsor and its registry class. `class` is what sponsor_type used to be asked for.

status.description: Lifecycle. `is_active` covers recruiting, enrolling-by-invitation, not-yet-recruiting and active-not-recruiting.

primary_completion_type.description: ACTUAL or ESTIMATED -- the difference between a fact and a plan.

design.description: The design descriptors an analyst expects at the top of a readout. `randomized` is null -- not false -- when CT.gov reports allocation NA, because inapplicable is not the same as a deliberate non-randomised design.

summary.description: One line, e.g. 'Phase 2, non-randomised, open-label, 3 parallel arms'.

arms.description: Arms as the registry gives them. `description` is null on ~20% of trials; that null is preserved so a readout can say the registry is silent rather than imply a distinction it cannot source.

interventions.description: Interventions with their descriptions retained -- this is where dose and schedule live (89.2% of trials), and it is what the v3 compact ingest discarded.

resolved.description: Acronym resolution from schema/regimens.py, when the name is a known regimen, shorthand or procedure. Absent when unknown -- never guessed.

agents.description: Distinct therapeutic agents with regimen acronyms expanded and brand names folded to generics. This is the list `modalities` is defined over. Procedures and delivery routes are excluded by kind, so a radiotherapy trial cannot acquire a drug modality.

has_results.description: Only 21.4% of this corpus. Stated so a reader knows whether outcome data exists at all -- v4 does not offer an outcome field, because it would be empty four times in five.

est_readout.description: Readout window computed from facts.status.primary_completion_date. Arithmetic, not judgement. ADR-0018 recorded Sonnet 5 overriding this mechanical rule with a realistic completion-to-publication lag -- a stronger model reasoning past an explicit instruction. The rule is now executed rather than requested.

indication.description: The disease setting in plain English, normalised from facts.conditions. Requires reading: registry condition strings are inconsistent, duplicated and sometimes list the population rather than the disease.

intervention_class.description: What kind of intervention this trial actually tests. Decide BEFORE modalities. 'drug/biologic' if any drug or biologic is given as anticancer therapy. CT.gov intervention types are a hint, not the answer: a trial can list a DRUG that is only premedication.

modalities.description: The DISTINCT therapeutic modalities among the agents in facts.agents, as an unordered set sorted alphabetically. Empty when intervention_class is not drug/biologic. This is pharmacology -- knowing trastuzumab emtansine is an antibody-drug conjugate is not something the record states.

primary_endpoint_type.description: Category of the primary outcome measure(s). Requires reading the outcome text, which is free prose.

risk_flags_judgement.description: Only the four flags that need reading the trial. The seven arithmetic flags are computed by schema/derive.py from the record (ADR-0022) and are not offered here.

investor_note.description: Two or three sentences an analyst could use, grounded in the facts tier. May reference design, arms and dosing now that they are available; must not restate numbers the facts tier already carries.
